title: The Chain on the Gate: an Engineer, a First Lady, and the Accusation Made from Inside the House
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Lima, the fourth child of Tomas Higuchi
stops.date_confidence: attested; neither the clinic nor the district of birth is recorded in any reachable source, so the pin is the city centroid
stops.campa: She is born on the twenty-sixth of April, 1950, the youngest of the four children of Tomas Higuchi and Seki Miyagawa, Japanese immigrants who have made their life in Peru. They give her a Peruvian first name and a Japanese second one, Susana Shizuko, and the two surnames in the Spanish order. The colony she is born into is small and commercial, old enough in the country to remember the wartime deportations and the sacking of Japanese shops in Lima. Where in the city she was born, no record says.
suggested_refs: Peruvian Nikkei community records of the postwar decade, Lima

stops.name: San Isidro, the colegio finished at fifteen
stops.date_confidence: the age of fifteen is attested and fixes the year near 1965; the source names only a state colegio called Senora de la Asuncion, and this coordinate belongs to the better known Nuestra Senora de la Asuncion in San Isidro, so the building may be the wrong one
stops.campa: She finishes secondary school at fifteen, two years ahead of the ordinary graduating age, in a state colegio named for Our Lady of the Assumption. That is the whole of it. The record does not keep what she read or who taught her, or what was made of a girl arriving at the end of the syllabus two years early. It keeps one thing more, which is where she goes next. She goes to an engineering faculty, where a Lima girl of 1965 was not sent, and where nobody in her family had gone before her.
suggested_refs: School registers of Lima state colegios for the 1964-1966 cohort

stops.name: La Victoria, the tire company called El Sol
stops.date_confidence: the employment is attested; no source dates it, and the year is placed by inference between school and marriage. District coordinate only, no street address found
stops.campa: The family settles in La Victoria, a dense working district east of the old centre, and before her marriage she takes work at the tire company El Sol. It is the ordinary employment of a young woman of the colony with numbers in her head and no capital of her own. What she was paid there, and how long she stayed, no source records. Thirty years on, when her husband campaigns for the presidency, part of the money that pays for it comes out of the accounts of her own company.
suggested_refs: Commercial registers of La Victoria, Lima, 1960s

stops.name: Rimac, the Universidad Nacional de Ingenieria
stops.date_confidence: the enrolment is attested; the source gives only the decade, so the year is placed by inference
stops.campa: She crosses the river to the engineering university at Rimac and reads civil engineering, specialising later in hydraulics, the discipline of moving water through a country that has too little of it on one side of the mountains and too much on the other. She is one of very few women in the lecture halls. Her father already knows Naoichi Fujimori, an immigrant of the same generation whose son teaches mathematics at the agrarian university across the city. The two fathers will make the introduction.
suggested_refs: Faculty of Civil Engineering records, Universidad Nacional de Ingenieria, Lima

stops.name: Lima Centro, the Capilla de la Virgen de la O
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of July, 1974, she marries Alberto Fujimori in the chapel of the Virgin of the O, attached to the baroque bulk of San Pedro on Jiron Ucayali. The courtship has been brief and was made through their fathers. Who came to the wedding, and what was said at it, is not recorded anywhere. What is known is the joining: two immigrant families of the same colony, one out of a tire district and the other out of a mathematics faculty, in a Catholic rite in the oldest Jesuit church of Lima.
suggested_refs: The Capilla de la Virgen de la O, Basilica y Convento de San Pedro, Cercado de Lima

stops.name: Lima, four children in six years
stops.date_confidence: attested for the first birth, which opens the sequence; the other three are attested to the month only
stops.campa: Keiko Sofia is born on the twenty-fifth of May, 1975, ten months after the wedding. Hiro Alberto follows in December 1976, Sachi Marcela in March 1979, Kenji Gerardo in May 1980. Four children inside six years, all born in Lima, while their mother is carrying the household's income on her own account. She is twenty-five at the first birth and thirty at the last. Of the four the civil registers keep the dates, and of the household around them they keep nothing at all.
suggested_refs: Peruvian civil birth registers, Lima, 1975-1980

stops.name: San Borja, the lots of the Empresa Constructora Fuji
stops.date_confidence: the company and the district are attested; no source gives a founding year or identifies a single lot, so the date is inferred and the coordinate is district-level
stops.campa: The couple open the Empresa Constructora Fuji and begin selling residential lots in San Borja, then a district of empty ground on Lima's eastern edge waiting for the middle class that will fill it. No registry document for the company has been found, and no single lot in the district can be named as one of theirs. The engineer of the pair is the wife. She surveys and she prices, and she is the one who deals with the municipality; through the second half of the decade she is the principal earner of the house.
suggested_refs: Registros Publicos entries for the Empresa Constructora Fuji, Lima

stops.name: Santiago de Surco, the second development
stops.date_confidence: attested to the 1970s only; the year is inferred and the coordinate is district-level, no specific development identified
stops.campa: Fuji builds again further south, in Santiago de Surco, houses rather than bare lots this time. No permit, plan or address for these houses has been located, and the coordinate is the district and nothing finer. She is a working engineer with four small children and a construction firm on the growing rim of a capital filling with people driven down from the sierra by war and drought. Her husband is still a teacher of mathematics, with no party and no public opinions on record.
suggested_refs: Municipal building permits, Santiago de Surco, Lima, 1970s

segments.name: Cambio 90 and the Casa de Pizarro

stops.name: Lima, the comedores populares of the Cambio 90 campaign
stops.date_confidence: the campaigning and the company funds are attested; the source names no individual comedor and gives no date, so the pin is general to Lima and the month is that of the first round
stops.campa: She does not want him to run. Cambio 90 is a party three months old with a tractor for an emblem, and the candidate is an agronomy dean whom the pollsters put at one per cent in January. She puts Fuji money into it anyway and walks the campaign herself, through the comedores populares of the poor districts where women cook in shifts for whole streets because no household can afford a pot of its own. In June he beats Mario Vargas Llosa in the second round, and on the twenty-eighth of July she becomes the wife of the President of Peru.
suggested_refs: Campaign records of Cambio 90, first and second rounds, 1990

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the twenty-eighth of July
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On national day her husband takes the oath and the family moves into the Casa de Pizarro on the Plaza Mayor, the government house that stands on the plot where the conqueror of Peru built his own and was cut down in it. She is forty years old and First Lady of a country in hyperinflation, with Sendero Luminoso bombing the pylons that light the room she sleeps in. The office she has just been given appears nowhere in the constitution of Peru; there is no oath for it and no term. She holds it for four years and one month.
suggested_refs: The Palacio de Gobierno del Peru, Plaza Mayor, Lima

stops.name: Lima, the Fundacion por los Ninos del Peru
stops.date_confidence: the presidency of the foundation is attested for 1990 without a month; the month is inferred and the foundation's office address was not found, so the pin is general
stops.campa: She is made president of the Fundacion por los Ninos del Peru, the charitable body through which the office of First Lady does most of what it is allowed to do. Its annual reports for these years have not been located, and even the address of its office is missing from the record. What is attested is the traffic: donations from abroad, much of it from Japan, moving toward children in a country where a third of them are malnourished. She reads the manifests line by line, the way she read a lot survey in San Borja.
suggested_refs: Fundacion por los Ninos del Peru, annual reports 1990-1994

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the clothing sent from Japan
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 1992; no source gives a day for the denunciation itself
stops.campa: She accuses her husband's sisters, Rosa and Juana Fujimori, of taking clothing donated from Japan through the association Apenkai, meant for the poor and for flood victims, and selling the good garments in street bazaars. The accusation is made in public, by the First Lady, against the President's own family, from inside the President's own house. It is March 1992, and she has been First Lady for twenty months. She is asked what loyalty she owes her husband's people, and she puts the question back.
stops.quote: Si por eso se me acusa de deslealtad, no sé a qué le llaman traición.
stops.quote_source: Susana Higuchi, 1992, quoted by Exitosa Noticias, 'Cuando Susana Higuchi denunció a los Fujimori por apropiarse donaciones de Japón'
suggested_refs: Apenkai donation manifests, Japanese aid to Peru, 1991-1992

stops.name: Lima, the chain on the gate
stops.date_confidence: the day is that of the El Tiempo report of 28 March 1992 carrying the Ebisui accusation; her statement about the gate is dated only to 1992
stops.campa: The accusation widens to a sister-in-law, Clorinda Ebisui, whom she says handed out the worst of the donated clothes under her own name. El Tiempo of Bogota prints it on the twenty-eighth of March, 1992, under a headline calling it a scandal in the president's family, and quotes her saying the thing outrages her. Then the doors close. The First Lady of Peru gives statements to reporters about the padlock on her own front railing: she cannot leave the residence, the order is her husband's, the gate is chained.
stops.quote: No me dejan salir de la residencia por orden de mi esposo, la reja está con cadena.
stops.quote_source: Susana Higuchi, 1992, quoted by Exitosa Noticias
suggested_refs: El Tiempo (Bogota), 'Escándalo en la familia del presidente Fujimori', 28 March 1992

stops.name: Lima, out of the palace after the autogolpe
stops.date_confidence: the date of the self-coup is attested; that the family was moved out of the Casa de Pizarro into army intelligence installations rests on Higuchi's own later account and was denied
stops.campa: On the fifth of April the President dissolves Congress, suspends the constitution and puts soldiers in the courts, and the country calls it the autogolpe. Higuchi's account of that week is that the family was taken out of the Casa de Pizarro and lodged in the installations of the Servicio de Inteligencia del Ejercito, the concrete star the city calls the Pentagonito, and that she had in effect already been seized in the days before the tanks moved. The government said otherwise.
suggested_refs: Cuartel General del Ejercito del Peru, San Borja, Lima

stops.name: San Borja, the basements of the SIE
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: her allegation covers roughly 1992 to 1994 and is placed here at its midpoint. The count and the sessions are her account alone, denied by Fujimori, and never adjudicated on the facts
stops.campa: What she says happened in the basements of army intelligence, she says for the rest of her life and never varies: a darkened room, interrogations, mistreatment, and a count she eventually put at more than five hundred separate occasions. She was First Lady of Peru for the whole of the period she describes. Her husband denied it and explained the marks on her body as the scars of moxibustion, the Japanese therapy of burning mugwort on the skin. No court ever ruled on which of the two was telling the truth.
stops.quote: fui torturada en más de 500 oportunidades
suggested_refs: Servicio de Inteligencia del Ejercito facilities, Lima, later the subject of criminal proceedings against Fujimori

stops.name: Palacio de Gobierno, the title passes to the daughter
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of August, 1994, she is formally stripped of the title and the duties of First Lady of Peru. The office is not in the constitution and cannot be resigned or dismissed in law, so the removal is done by announcement, and it takes effect on the day it is announced. The functions pass to Keiko Sofia Fujimori, nineteen years old, the daughter born ten months after the wedding at San Pedro. Higuchi is forty-four years old. Keiko holds the office until the twenty-first of November, 2000.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiko_Fujimori, on the tenure of 23 August 1994 to 21 November 2000

stops.name: Lima, the interview given to Spanish radio
stops.date_confidence: attested to 20 October 1994 by the El Comercio profile; the outlet is described only as Spanish radio
stops.campa: Two months after losing the title she gives an interview to a Spanish radio station and calls her husband a tyrant and his government corrupt, in a country where the government has recently suspended the congress and won a war on the press. She says he fears her and therefore makes her life impossible, and that she is still married to him while fighting for a different road. Her fight is over principles, she says, and not over marital quarrels. Asked what she is risking, she says she does not even fear death.
stops.quote: He visto pasar la corrupción por el Palacio Presidencial.
stops.quote_source: Susana Higuchi, interview to Spanish radio, 20 October 1994, cited in El Comercio, Carlos Batalla, 'Susana Higuchi, ex primera dama de la Nación'
suggested_refs: El Comercio archive, Carlos Batalla, profile of Susana Higuchi

stops.name: Lima, the Palacio de Justicia and the end of the marriage
stops.date_confidence: the divorce action falls in 1994 and the Lima tribunal's formalisation in 1995; no source gives the month or day of the ruling, so the date defaults to January
stops.campa: The divorce is filed in 1994 with an accusation attached to it: kidnapping, and torture in the basements of army intelligence. In 1995 the tribunal of Lima makes it final. The marriage that began in a Jesuit chapel eight blocks away ends in a building on the Paseo de la Republica, and the woman walking out of it leaves the residence and the title along with the husband. What was argued in the courtroom is nowhere in the reachable record, and neither the month nor the day of the ruling is given.
suggested_refs: Palacio de Justicia de Lima, Av. Paseo de la Republica

stops.name: Lima, the Movimiento Armonia Siglo XXI struck from the ballot
stops.date_confidence: contradiction left standing: the Spanish account puts the blocked presidential ticket in 1995 and blames the electoral authorities, while the English account dates the party's disqualification to December 1994 on the ground of insufficient signatures. Month and day are unknown either way
stops.campa: She founds her own movement, Armonia Siglo XXI, and enters it in coalition as Frempol for the presidency of Peru against the man she was married to. The ticket is invalidated. She turns to a congressional candidacy and that is invalidated too. The sources do not agree on why: one says the electoral authorities, controlled by the government, struck her from the ballot, the other says the party never gathered the signatures a party needs. What both agree on is that she did not appear on it.
suggested_refs: Resolutions of the Jurado Nacional de Elecciones on the Armonia Siglo XXI-Frempol ticket, 1994-1995

stops.name: Lima, the mayoral candidacy rejected
stops.date_confidence: the source places the rejected Lima mayoral bid later in 1995 without a month, so the month here is a placeholder; the source also attributes the rejection to ONPE, though candidate registration is ordinarily the function of the JNE
stops.campa: Struck off the presidential ballot and off the congressional list, she files for the mayoralty of Lima. That candidacy is rejected too, on the ground that the filing requirements were not met. Three filings in one year and three refusals at the counter, none of them made by a voter. The source attributes this last rejection to the ONPE, though the registration of candidates is ordinarily the business of the Jurado Nacional de Elecciones. She is forty-five and holds no office.
suggested_refs: Electoral filings for the Lima municipal contest, 1995

stops.name: Washington, the Commission takes her case
stops.date_confidence: the report's date is attested; Higuchi is the named petitioner, but she is not documented as physically present at the Commission, and the Commission's own text was not retrieved for this file
stops.campa: Four years on, the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights issues Report No. 119/99 in Case 11.428, Susana Higuchi Miyagawa, and concludes that Peru violated her political rights when it barred her candidacies of 1995. The finding lands in Washington while the government it names is still in office in Lima and about to run for a third term. It changes nothing about the 1995 ballots, and the government wins its third term the following April. Whether she was in the room to hear the finding read, no source says.
suggested_refs: IACHR Report No. 119/99, Case 11.428, Susana Higuchi Miyagawa, 6 October 1999

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, sworn in for the Frente Independiente Moralizador
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Fernando Olivera puts her third on the list of the Frente Independiente Moralizador and the country returns her with 126,451 votes, the ninth-highest personal tally in the race. The election of 2000 is run in a single national district, so she is not elected for Lima but for Peru entire. On the twenty-sixth of July she takes the oath in the chamber on Avenida Abancay. Her husband dissolved that congress with tanks in 1992 and had it rebuilt afterwards to his own measure.
suggested_refs: Official results of the 2000 Peruvian congressional election, single national district

stops.name: Palacio de Justicia, the Marcha de los Cuatro Suyos
stops.date_confidence: the march ran from 26 to 29 July 2000, with 28 July as its central day and the crowd of some 250,000 attached principally to the 27th; her participation is attested in her own article and is not mentioned in the accounts of the march itself
stops.campa: Four columns of marchers walk into the centre of Lima from four directions, named for the four suyos of the Inca division of the world, to stand against a third term nobody believes was won cleanly. The platform is raised near the Palacio de Justicia and the crowd on the second day runs to some quarter of a million people. She is in it, ten years after walking the soup kitchens for him. Her own account is the only one that puts her there; the histories of the march do not mention her at all.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcha_de_los_Cuatro_Suyos

stops.name: Plaza San Martin, the first vladivideo at the Hotel Bolivar
stops.date_confidence: the date, the venue and the content of the release are attested; the account of the vladivideos credits the press conference to Luis Iberico and Frank Cayo and does not name her, so her presence there rests on her own article alone
stops.campa: In a room of the Gran Hotel Bolivar on the Plaza San Martin, her party colleagues play a videotape to the press. On it Vladimiro Montesinos, the intelligence adviser who runs the government's back rooms, is counting out cash to the congressman Alberto Kouri to buy his defection. It is the first of the vladivideos, and within two months it brings down the presidency, the adviser and the whole apparatus. She has been a congresswoman for seven weeks.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladivideos, on the press conference of 14 September 2000

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, the censure and Valentin Paniagua
stops.date_confidence: the censure of Martha Hildebrandt and Paniagua's election to the presidency of Congress fall in mid-November 2000; the exact day of her own vote is not recorded in the sources
stops.campa: The government's majority breaks apart vote by vote in the weeks after the vladivideo. She votes to censure Martha Hildebrandt out of the presidency of the chamber, and then for Valentin Paniagua into it; the day of her own vote is not recorded. Days later Fujimori's resignation arrives from Tokyo by fax and is refused, so that he can be removed for moral incapacity instead. The presidency of Congress becomes the presidency of the Republic in the third week of November 2000.
suggested_refs: Diario de Debates, Congreso de la Republica del Peru, November 2000

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, re-elected for Lima
stops.date_confidence: the re-election for the 2001-2006 term is attested; 26 July is the swearing-in of that congress
stops.campa: She is returned for a second term, this time for the constituency of Lima, still with the Frente Independiente Moralizador. The congress she enters now is the one that will try, in committee after committee, to establish what was done in the country between 1990 and 2000: the intelligence payments, the death squad, the sterilisations, the vanished tapes. She sits in it as a legislator and as a witness, which are two different jobs, and the record of her work as the first is thin.
suggested_refs: Congressional record of the 2001-2006 Peruvian legislature

stops.name: Lima, the twelve and a half million from Japan
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 2001 as her allegation; it is not an adjudicated finding, and no day is given
stops.campa: She states publicly that her former husband took a donation of twelve and a half million dollars sent from Japan. It is the accusation she made from inside the palace nine years earlier over sacks of secondhand clothing, made now from a seat in the legislature rather than from behind a chained gate. No court has ever established that the money moved as she said. The statement is dated to July 2001; no day is given for it, and nothing was published alongside it.
suggested_refs: Japanese official development assistance to Peru, 1990s, and the Apenkai channel

stops.name: Lima, the order she says was given against Alan Garcia
stops.date_confidence: the date is that of the El Tiempo report carrying the statements; the underlying allegation is hers and was denied
stops.campa: She tells the press that on the day of the autogolpe her husband and Montesinos gave an order to kill the former president Alan Garcia, and that she warned Garcia, who left the country and stayed out of it for nine years. Garcia by then is back in Peru and has just lost a presidential runoff; he will be elected president again in 2006. The claim is hers alone and was denied. Her account of why she made the telephone call does not mention politics. She says she did not want to be party to a murder.
stops.quote: Yo no quise ser partícipe de un asesinato.
stops.quote_source: Susana Higuchi, quoted in El Tiempo (Bogota), 'Hay que matar a Alan', 20 September 2001
suggested_refs: El Tiempo (Bogota), 'Hay que matar a Alan', 20 September 2001

stops.name: Lima, a mass for the dead of La Cantuta
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the source records only that she took part in a mass held by the relatives of the La Cantuta victims, with neither date nor venue. The year is placed inside her congressional service and the pin is the city, not the university, which the source never names as the site
stops.campa: In July 1992 a death squad of the army took nine students and a professor out of the university at La Cantuta in the night; their bodies were burned and buried in two places outside the city and found by a magazine following a map. Their families keep saying mass for them year after year. The former First Lady of the government whose intelligence service ordered it goes to one of those masses. Which mass, in which church, in which year, the record does not say. She sits with the families through it.
suggested_refs: The La Cantuta massacre of 18 July 1992 and the Grupo Colina proceedings

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, the bench of Peru Ahora
stops.date_confidence: the move is attested to 2005; the month is not given in the sources, so the date defaults to January
stops.campa: She resigns from the Frente Independiente Moralizador over disagreements inside it and crosses to the bench called Peru Ahora, led by Luis Guerrero Figueroa. It is her third political home in ten years, after her own struck-off movement and Olivera's front. She had entered the chamber as the emblematic witness of the previous decade and finishes it as a backbencher moving between parliamentary groups. The sources give the year of the move and not the month, and they do not say what the disagreements were about.
suggested_refs: Parliamentary group registers, Congreso de la Republica, 2005

stops.name: Congreso de la Republica, the end of the second term
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Her term ends on the twenty-sixth of July, 2006, six years to the day after she first took the oath. She does not stand again, and she never holds public office afterwards. Fujimori is at this point in Chile, in custody, awaiting the extradition that will bring him back the following year to be tried and convicted for La Cantuta, for Barrios Altos, and for the kidnappings carried out from the building where she says she was held. She is fifty-six years old.
suggested_refs: Congressional service record of Susana Higuchi, 2000-2006

stops.name: Lima, mother and daughter in public again
stops.date_confidence: the reconciliation is attested to 2016 without a month, so the date defaults to January
stops.campa: After years of estrangement she appears again beside Keiko, who is now leading the polls for the presidency of Peru. Nothing in the sources explains the terms on which this was settled between the two of them, or what either agreed not to say about the years in between. The year is 2016; the month is not given. The daughter installed in her place at nineteen is now forty, running as the head of her father's movement, and her mother is on the platform beside her.
suggested_refs: Coverage of the Fuerza Popular campaign of 2016

stops.name: Barranca, on the campaign road north of Lima
stops.date_confidence: the swing through Barranca, Pativilca and Paramonga is attested to the second-round campaign of 2016; the report carrying the quotations shows no day-level dateline, so the day is a placeholder
stops.campa: Campaigning through the sugar towns of the coast north of Lima, she answers the charge that her daughter's schooling was paid with money that came from somewhere it should not have. Her answer is a family accounting, delivered flat, and it puts her own father in the middle of the ledger. In the same breath she turns on the rival candidate, Pedro Pablo Kuczynski, and says he has deceived the whole of Peru with millions in play and has the nerve to stand for the presidency.
stops.quote: Las enseñanzas de mis hijos han sido pagadas íntegramente por mi padre. Todos los años y de todos mis hijos. Mi padre era millonario.
stops.quote_source: Susana Higuchi, campaigning in Barranca, Pativilca and Paramonga, 2016, quoted by RPP Noticias
suggested_refs: RPP Noticias, 'Susana Higuchi: Mi padre pagó por los estudios de mis hijos'

stops.name: San Borja, the grandchildren
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested; the month is not given in the sources, and the household address is not published, so the pin is district-level
stops.campa: Keiko is taken into preventive detention in the Odebrecht investigation, and the children are left. Their grandmother takes them. She is sixty-eight, a retired congresswoman, and she is keeping house for a candidate's family while the candidate is in a cell, in the same city where she once told reporters there was a chain on her own gate. The district is San Borja, where she sold the first lots of Constructora Fuji forty years before. The household address has never been published.
suggested_refs: Proceedings in the Peruvian Odebrecht investigation, 2018

stops.name: Lima, the last campaign
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2021 without a month; the Peruvian election ran in April and June of that year, and no single appearance of hers is dated in the sources
stops.campa: She backs Keiko's third run for the presidency, which ends in June in a defeat of forty-four thousand votes and a long refusal to concede. It is the last political act of her life. The woman who once tried to run against Alberto Fujimori, and was struck from three ballots in a single year, spends her final campaign on the platforms of the movement he founded, standing behind their daughter. No single appearance of hers in it is dated in the sources, and no speech of hers from it is quoted. She is seventy-one.
suggested_refs: Coverage of the Peruvian general election of 2021

stops.name: San Borja, the Oncosalud clinic
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: She dies of cancer on the eighth of December, 2021, at the Oncosalud clinic on Avenida Guardia Civil in San Borja, seventy-one years old. Her daughter announces it publicly the same day, in the language of a family and not of a campaign. Alberto Fujimori is alive, imprisoned in the Barbadillo penitentiary at the eastern edge of the same city, serving twenty-five years. He was convicted in 2009 of the killings at Barrios Altos and La Cantuta and of kidnappings carried out by the intelligence service.
stops.quote: Después de una dura lucha contra el cáncer, nuestra madre, Susana Higuchi acaba de partir al encuentro de Dios.
stops.quote_source: Keiko Fujimori, public announcement of her mother's death, 8 December 2021
suggested_refs: Oncosalud, Av. Guardia Civil 571, San Borja, Lima

stops.name: Jesus Maria, the wake at the Parroquia Santa Maria
stops.date_confidence: the wake is attested to December 2021; no source gives the day, and it is placed here on the day after her death
stops.campa: The wake is held at the Parroquia Santa Maria Madre de la Iglesia on Avenida Gregorio Escobedo in Jesus Maria. No source gives the day of it, or the names of those who spoke. Condolences come from the sitting president Pedro Castillo, from members of congress across the parties, and from two former presidents, Ollanta Humala and Pedro Pablo Kuczynski. From a platform in Barranca five years earlier she had called Kuczynski a man who deceived the whole of Peru.
suggested_refs: Parroquia Santa Maria Madre de la Iglesia, Av. Gregorio Escobedo, Jesus Maria, Lima

stops.name: Huachipa, the Cementerio Campo Fe
stops.date_confidence: December 2021 is attested; no source gives the day of burial, which is placed here immediately after the wake, and the plot is not published
stops.campa: She is buried at the Campo Fe cemetery at Huachipa, upriver from Lima on the Rimac, in ground that was cane and cotton fields when she was born, on the road that runs up the valley toward the sierra. She is not cremated. The hydraulics engineer trained at the university across the water is put into the floodplain of the same river, a few kilometres above the city she never left. She was seventy-one, and every address the record gives for her is in Lima or its valley. The plot number is not published.
